Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks for the time today — quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery on latency/throughput and regional routing requirements. If I missed anything, flag it and we’ll update.

Recap (what we heard):
- Target interactive latency: P95 ~<200ms (US), ~<250ms (EU), ~<300ms (APAC) for 1–2k concurrent users.
- Throughput: expected steady-state ~20 reqs/s during peak (chat messages), spiky bursts up to ~120 reqs/s.
- Concurrency: typical per-user concurrency is low (1–2), but backend concurrency for batching is expected ~64–128 parallel inferences.
- Streaming: client expects streaming/chunked token delivery for chat (low-latency partial tokens).
- Data residency: EU production traffic and logs must remain in EU; APAC requires local processing for a subset of customers (data residency constraint).
- Compliance: Finova requires audit logs and retention policy (we discussed 7 years for some records).

Action items / next steps:
1) Rishi to confirm recommended deployment topology and whether we can meet the P95 targets with the recommended model config + routing. (Rishi — can you provide expected GPU counts and batching guidance?)
2) Marissa to send a draft SLO proposal + network diagram (attached).
3) Laura to follow up with procurement/contract ask list and DocuSign link for PoC SOW.
4) Schedule a technical PoC kickoff (preferably next week) — propose Wed 03/11 10am PT.

Attachments: redwood-slo-proposal.pdf (draft), network-topology.png

Thanks — talk soon.

On Mon, Mar 2, 2026 at 3:12 PM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Recap (what we heard):
> - Target interactive latency: P95 ~<200ms (US), ~<250ms (EU), ~<300ms (APAC) for 1–2k concurrent users.
> - Throughput: expected steady-state ~20 reqs/s during peak (chat messages), spiky bursts up to ~120 reqs/s.

Quick technical notes / initial capacity guidance:
- Regional routing: We can deploy replicas in US, EU, and APAC regions and route by user geography with sticky routing for session affinity. For stringent EU data residency we’ll ensure requests + logs stay within the EU cluster.
- Latency feasibility: For P95 <200ms on interactive generations we recommend:
  * Model: rwd-large-v2 (quantized) or a comparable low-latency variant.
  * Dedicated capacity: reserve 4–8 A100-class GPUs per region for the initial PoC (depends on concurrency profile). With batching tuned to 16–32 and KV caching enabled we expect to hit P95 ~120–220ms in US for short-turn chat prompts (~<256 tokens).
- Throughput / concurrency: With the above config, steady 20 reqs/s easily covered; bursts to 120 reqs/s require autoscale headroom or burst capacity (we can configure burst pools). For very high sustained concurrency we’d recommend reserved Dedicated pools to avoid queueing.
- Streaming: We support chunked token streaming (server-sent events / chunked HTTP). Streaming adds ~5–20ms overhead per chunk but preserves perceived latency — recommend smaller chunks (~20–40 tokens) for first-byte speed.
- Fallbacks & graceful degradation: If APAC region constrained, we can failover to a lower-cost model variant in-region or route to nearest region with session-level consent.
- Data residency / logs: For EU-only residency we’ll host compute and log storage in EU (customer-managed S3/GCS option or Redwood-managed EU storage). Audit logs retention policy configurable (we can set retention to 7 years for the classes you specified), will need procurement signoff for long-term storage costs.

Deliverables I’ll prepare by EOD Tue: rough GPU count + expected P95 estimates per-region (US/EU/APAC) and recommended batching/quantization profile.

Thanks Marissa / Rishi —

This is helpful. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we lock PoC dates:
1) Can you provide the concrete P95 numbers per-region using the suggested config (i.e., datasets of ~200–300 token prompts) — we need an SLA proposal to present to our ops/security team.
2) For streaming: we require true low-latency streaming (we can tolerate 10–20ms per-chunk overhead but first-token must arrive quickly). Will Redwood’s streaming meet that consistently?
3) Data residency: EU data must not leave the EU for processing or logs. For APAC customers (Japan/Australia) we need local processing. Is the private deployment (VPC) necessary for APAC residency or can hosted Dedicated in an APAC region suffice?
4) Procurement: we’ll need a short PoC SOW + a list of required network/IPs and certs for allowlisting. Can you send a DocuSign for the PoC SOW?

If you can send the P95 table + recommended GPU counts and a proposed PoC SOW by EOD today we’ll aim to start PoC next week.

Samir — thanks, good questions. See attached proposal (redwood-slo-proposal.pdf) and network diagram (network-topology.png). High-level answers below; Rishi will share the P95 table shortly.

Quick answers:
- P95 numbers: Draft estimates attached; Rishi will validate but expect P95 in US ~120–180ms, EU ~160–240ms, APAC ~200–320ms depending on final model and token length. We’ll include the per-region breakdown in the tech note.
- Streaming: We support SSE / chunked HTTP and have customers in production using it with median first-byte times well under 100ms — for your requirements we’ll prioritize smaller chunking and session affinity to keep first-token latency low.
- APAC residency: Hosted Dedicated in APAC regions is usually sufficient to keep data in-region, but for contractual/regulatory reasons some customers prefer Private (VPC/on-prem) in APAC. We can run the PoC on Hosted Dedicated in APAC first and discuss Private options if needed.
- DocuSign & procurement: Laura, could you share the PoC SOW + DocuSign link (per Samir’s ask)?
